value.text: Many of the issues can be organized around the following two questions: Is existence a property of individuals? and Assuming that existence is a property of individuals, are there individuals that lack it?
Everything which exists is called an entity.
that which is perceived or known or inferred to have its own distinct existence (living or nonliving)

Every entity in Wikidata is implicitly an instance of (P31) entity (Q35120).  These implicit instance of (P31) statements are not all observable in Wikidata.  In general no item should explicitly be an instance of (P31) entity (Q35120).  Only a small predefined set of items should be subclasses of (P279) of entity. For any regular entity the implicit relationship suffices even if there is no other class that can be found for the entity to be an instance of (P31).
That which is considered to exist as a separate entity, quality or concept.

that which is perceived or known or inferred to have its own distinct existence (living or nonliving)
An independently existing thing (living or nonliving).
